title.narrative: Emergency MPCA to Vulnerable and Crises Affected Households in the West Bank

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project will provide one round of Emergency MPCA to 410 displaced and highly vulnerable households (approximately 2,050 individuals) in Tulkarm, and Nur Al Shams Refugee Camps in Tulkarem governorate to help them meet urgent basic needs and maintain dignity throughout the ongoing displacement that has been unfolding since January 2025. ltbrgtThe intervention is fully aligned with the 2026 Cash Working Group (CWG) priorities and transfer-value guidance and responds directly to Flash Appeal priorities informed by assessments that highlight severe displacement impacts and heightened socio-economic vulnerability in the northern West Bank. Assistance will be delivered using the CWG-recommended MPCA transfer value for the West Bank (currently 1,755 ILS/HH), representing 80% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), enabling households to cover critical expenditures during the crisis. ltbrgtTulkarm and Nur Shams have experienced sustained military operations, increased settler violence, movement restrictions, and infrastructure demolitions since October 2023. Displaced households have experienced severe or total damage to their homes, they have lost personal belongings and livelihoods, leaving them with no means to generate income and reliant on negative coping strategies to meet basic needs. Across all target locations, families face shrinking livelihood options, limited access to governmental services and humanitarian aid, and high protection risks due to frequent military operations, search and arrest operations, and an increasingly coercive environment driving displacements of individuals. ltbrgtThese conditions amplify the need for flexible, rapid-response assistance that can reach affected populations despite access constraints. In response, CRS proposes to provide one-round of MPCA to 410 households over a 4-month period so they can meet their urgent basic needs. The intervention is further in line with the MPC Cluster Objective RA4 2025 that ensures internally displaced people (IPDs) in the North of the West Bank, can meet their most urgent and essential needs in a dignified and flexible manner. ltbrgtAs per recent assessment data, 25% of households are headed by women or elderly individuals, and 16% of households include at least one person with a disability. Thus, underlining the need for interventions that address heightened vulnerabilities and accessibility barriers. As such, targeting will prioritise women- and elderly-headed households, households with persons with disabilities, and families with limited or no income. ltbrgtCRS will implement the proposed intervention with ltbgtPartners for Sustainable Development (PSD)lt/bgt in Tulkarm covering Tulkarm and Nur Al Shams refugee camps. ltbgtPSD lt/bgthas been in operation since 2021 and maintains an active operational presence in Tulkarm. CRS and local partner’s strong community relations and relationship with the authorities will facilitate the approval of activities and support safety and security. ltbrgtThe cash delivery mechanism used under the program is considered the most accessible for most vulnerable IDPs, as it offers people the option to cash out at any participating CRS vendor, limiting the distance they have to travel, as well as the option of creating an e-wallet to receive assistance in digital form. ltbrgtDisaggregated data for all recipient households will be collected during beneficiary identification, including sex of the recipient and whether the household includes persons with disabilities. Monitoring data will also capture similar data to enable disaggregation of monitoring findings by vulnerability profile. ltbrgtlt/pgt
